docs.title: Comprehensive Stroke Center Management
docs.text:
A practical operating system for Medical Directors and Associate Medical Directors who must build, run, improve, grow, and elevate an academic CSC to sustained national and international standing.

Start with Day One How to use this handbook Choose by role

Eight parts · 46 chapters · operational playbooks · evidence register · living monthly update · version 2026.08.2

docs.title: Opening
docs.text:
An academic Comprehensive Stroke Center is not a certificate on a wall. It is a 24/7 regional capability: hyperacute reperfusion, hemorrhagic and complex cerebrovascular care, neurocritical care, a dedicated stroke unit, a telestroke and transfer network, a quality system that can see itself in near real time, a training pipeline, and a research enterprise that changes practice. The same system owns four designed products that academic CSCs often leave implicit: in-hospital and perioperative stroke, goals-of-care and death-by-neurologic-criteria pathways, a TIA and minor-stroke clinic, and an elective cerebrovascular program. The Medical Director is the person who must hold those pieces as one system.

This handbook is written for that job. It treats certification as a floor, not a destination. It treats volume as a responsibility, not a trophy. It treats academic productivity as part of the clinical mission, not a weekend hobby. Every chapter is designed to be used in a meeting, a huddle, a survey week, a budget cycle, or a 90-day turnaround.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
Versioning is a calendar / SemVer hybrid:

  • YYYY.MM — monthly currency drop (example: 2026.08).
  • YYYY.MM.n — same-month correction (example: 2026.08.1).
  • There is no separate marketing major version. The year is the major. The month is the minor. The patch is only for in-month fixes.

See Living Document & Monthly Update Protocol for how a version is cut. See Evidence Register for the claims that must move with the version.

docs.title: 2026.08.2 — accuracy + comprehensiveness pass
docs.text:
Released: 18 August 2026 Register last verified: 2026-08-18

Same-month accuracy and comprehensiveness pass after 2026.08.1. No invented volume requirements. No author names, licenses, or disclaimers added.

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text:
• AIS fever locked at >37.5 °C (2026 AIS §4.4). Retired the ≥38.0 AIS cut. ICH INTERACT3 remains ≤37.5 °C. Operationally both mean treat at >37.5 — same number, different order-set.
  • Glucose: treat hypoglycemia <60 mg/dL; persistent hyperglycemia 140–180 mg/dL is still reasonable; intensive 80–130 is not recommended.
  • Post-reperfusion BP tables locked: pre-IVT <185/110; post-IVT 24 h <180/105; intensive SBP <140 after IVT is not recommended; after successful EVT, intensive SBP <140 is harmful and not recommended.
  • BAO EVT: strong recommendation within 24 hours if NIHSS ≥10. Do not apply DAWN/DEFUSE perfusion maps. Effectiveness not well established for NIHSS 6–9.
  • CSTK-03 / CSTK-04 / CSTK-06 specification lock: Hunt and Hess for SAH and ICH Score for ICH (prior to surgery or within 6 hours of arrival if no surgery); CSTK-04 initiation ≥90% internal (100% eligible tracked is a different metric); first nimodipine within 24 hours of arrival, enteral only, never IV.
  • Door-to-device ≠ puncture: Advanced Therapy door-to-device is arrival to first pass with the thrombectomy device; CSTK-09 is arrival to skin puncture.
  • EMTALA recipient-hospital posture locked for transfer and load-share language.
  • 2021 secondary prevention: revascularization within 2 weeks (Class 2a); LDL-C <70 statin ± ezetimibe (Class 1); clinic BP <130/80 (Class 1) unless ICH/aSAH/maternal tables apply.
  • Honor Roll / Elite / Elite Plus / Advanced Therapy remain published award criteria, not CSC certification floors. Award cuts sit in an Award column; internal stretch sits in Internal. Elite may be a labeled internal aim.
  • Operating-rhythm lock residual cleanup: daily huddle → weekly ops → monthly quality → quarterly stroke executive.

docs.title: Comprehensiveness
docs.text:

  • TNK 0.4 / cardiac-card refuse checkbox added to the paper code-stroke packet, after-action AGENT line, survey posters, DTN audit, and late-DTN worksheet.
  • Advanced Therapy 50% qualifier restored on the EVT SOP. aSAH SOP expanded to the securing-clock steps. KPI library reserves P-14–P-17 and P-19 (P-18 unused; ICH temperature in P-36). Code-stroke SOP points in-house steps to Chapter 43.

docs.title: 2026.08.1 — accuracy, special populations, and design pass
docs.text:
Released: 18 August 2026 Register last verified: 2026-08-18

Same-month correction after a multi-swarm review of the initial public release. No invented volume requirements. No author names, licenses, or disclaimers added.

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text:
• Named tenecteplase 0.4 mg/kg as Class 3 – No Benefit (2026 AIS) in the IVT chapter, TNK SOP, ready-room check, glossary, and ER-AIS-2026-02b. Cardiac-strength cards are a stop-the-line event.
  • Separated DAWN (6–24 h) from DEFUSE 3 (6–16 h). Restored the 50% qualifier on Advanced Therapy door-to-device in the hyperacute opening.
  • Split STK-6 (discharged on statin) from GWTG achievement #7 (intensive statin) in the KPI library (P-29 / P-29b).
  • Unified AIS unit fever at ≥38.0 °C and reserved INTERACT3 ≤37.5 °C for ICH, labeled as trial-bundle. Superseded the same day by 2026.08.2 (>37.5 °C for AIS).
  • Locked one 90-day mRS clock: enroll at discharge, first attempt day 60, second day 75, close the spec window.
  • Corrected the CSTK v2026B posting date (02/06/2026, not 08/08/2025) and retargeted CSTK-01/10/11 MIF links to v2026B.
  • Updated the January 2026 FDA CDS guidance: time-critical is a Criterion 4 factor, not an automatic Criterion 3 device trigger (ER-FDA-CDS-2026).
  • Locked operating-rhythm names: daily huddle → weekly ops → monthly quality → quarterly stroke executive. Retired the competing “stroke operations committee.”
  • Honor Roll / Elite / Elite Plus / Advanced Therapy labeled as published award criteria, not CSC certification floors.

docs.title: Comprehensiveness
docs.text:
• New Chapter 42 — Special Populations: CVT (2024 AHA statement), maternal stroke (2026 AHA statement), pediatric receiving compact, plus dated LVAD/ECMO and sickle-cell pointers. No invented doses or exchange thresholds.
  • Pediatric AIS night card in the IVT chapter. PFO and carotid revascularization rows in transitions. Fillable large-core EVT card. Time-banded ICH first-hour mermaid. aSAH nimodipine + securing SOP (SOP-CSC-SAH-001).
  • New KPIs P-36–P-39 (ICH bundle, nimodipine clock, securing clock, large-core review). Morning huddle map so 07:00 unit charge and 08:00 OS huddle are not two competing standups.
  • Glossary expanded (CVT, PFO, ESUS, TIA, BAO, DCI, EVD, CEA/CAS/TCAR, just culture, teach-back, stroke program manager vs ACGME PD, drip-and-drive, CDS/SaMD, StrokeNet National Coordinating Center).

Initial public release of Comprehensive Stroke Center Management, an operational handbook for Medical Directors and Associate Medical Directors of U.S. academic Comprehensive Stroke Centers.

docs.title: What shipped
docs.text:
Site and navigation

  • MkDocs Material handbook with eight parts plus a reference section.
  • Home, how-to-use, and role-based reading paths.
  • Search, light/dark theme, and mermaid diagrams as operating pictures.

Part II — Leadership and governance (nav targets)

Part VII — Strategy and elite performance (nav targets)

Part VIII — Playbooks and toolkits (this drop)

  • 38 First 90 Days and Year One — week-by-week 90-day plan, quarters 2–4, first-year scorecard, stakeholder map, do-not-break list, survey year vs build year.
  • 39 Checklists, Agendas, and Cadence — paste-ready huddle, weekly ops, monthly quality, quarterly executive, annual offsite, after-action, transfer intake, survey week, escalation card.

Reference

  • Evidence Register — sourced claims for the 2026 AIS guideline, CSTK v2026B (including CSTK-07 retired), STK/STK-OP, GWTG and Target: Stroke tiers, April 2, 2025 aSAH volume announcement (20 → 10), 2022 ICH and 2023 aSAH guidelines, HERMES numbers, TNK dose, StrokeNet, and QI/HRO methods. Last-verified date 2026-08-18.
  • Glossary — 80+ CSC operating terms with operational definitions.
  • Living Document Protocol — first-of-month checklist, sources to re-open, chapter-patch rules, register-row rules, YYYY.MM versioning, pointer to repository-root AGENTS.md prompts.
  • This changelog.

docs.title: Evidence locked in 2026.08
docs.text:
• 2026 AHA/ASA AIS guideline (Stroke 2026;57(8):e316–e436; DOI 10.1161/STR.0000000000000513): TNK 0.25 mg/kg max 25 mg or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg; treat disabling deficits within 4.5 h regardless of NIHSS; dual-eligible IVT plus EVT without delaying thrombectomy; MSU endorsed; first pediatric AIS recommendations; glucose and dysphagia updates.
  • CSTK Specifications Manual v2026B (posted 02/06/2026; 3Q–4Q 2026 discharges): IDs 01–06 and 08–12 active; CSTK-07 not in the current set; CSTK-01 exclusions as registered.
  • GWTG-Stroke public criteria (last reviewed 9 September 2022): 85% on each of seven achievement measures; Bronze 90 days / Silver 12 months / Gold 24 months; Target: Stroke Honor Roll 75% DTN ≤60, Elite 85% DTN ≤60, Elite Plus 75% DTN ≤45 and 50% DTN ≤30; Advanced Therapy 50% door-to-device ≤90 direct / ≤60 transfer; Target: Type 2 Diabetes composite ≥80% for 12 months.
  • The April 2, 2025 Joint Commission announcement reduced the annual aSAH volume criterion to 10. Other volume numbers remain confirm live against the E-App / CSC eligibility table. Historical “25 IV thrombolysis cases” is labeled historical.
  • HERMES: mRS 0–2 46.0% vs 26.5%; NNT 2.6 for ≥1-point mRS shift.

docs.title: Intentional absences
docs.text:
• No author by-lines, personal names of handbook creators, or institutional affiliations of individuals.
  • No authorship headers, legal-header files, or disclaimer language in the published pages.
  • No proprietary data from a named hospital or health system.
  • No invented current EVT or IVT volume requirements.

docs.title: Evidence Register
docs.text:
This register is the handbook’s source-of-truth file for high-consequence claims. Every numeric threshold, measure ID, dose, volume criterion, and trial result used in operations chapters is listed here with a primary source, a verified extraction, a last-verified date, and a status.

Do not update a chapter number without updating the matching row. Do not introduce a new numeric claim in any chapter without adding a row.

docs.title: How to read a row
docs.text: Column Meaning ID Stable handbook identifier. Do not reuse a retired ID. Claim The operational statement the handbook is allowed to make. Chapter Primary chapters that depend on the claim. Primary source Full citation plus URL and/or DOI. Verified extraction The exact fact pulled from the source — not a paraphrase that drifts. Last verified Date the source was opened and the extraction confirmed. Status active (use), confirm live (re-open the primary before quoting), historical (do not treat as current requirement), retired (do not use).

docs.title: Currency protocol
docs.text:
1. On the first business day of each month, run the checklist in Living Document & Monthly Update Protocol.
  2. Re-open every source marked confirm live and every source whose issuing body published in the prior 90 days.
  3. If an extraction still matches, update Last verified only.
  4. If an extraction changed, patch the listed chapters, change the claim and extraction, set status, and add a changelog entry.
  5. If a measure ID is removed by the issuer (example: CSTK-07 is not in v2026B or v2027A), mark the row retired and purge the ID from agendas, dashboards, and posters the same week.
  6. Version the handbook as YYYY.MM after the monthly pass. Use YYYY.MM.1 only for a same-month correction.
  7. Use the repository-root AGENTS.md monthly evidence-refresh prompt to run the pass.

Current handbook version: 2026.08.2. Register-wide last-verified date for the initial public release: 2026-08-18. Accuracy and special-populations pass 2026.08.1, and same-day 2026.08.2 accuracy + comprehensiveness pass, on 2026-08-18.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Operational definitions for Comprehensive Stroke Center management. Definitions are written for Medical Directors, program managers, and quality analysts. Where a Joint Commission or AHA construct is named, the live manual or recognition page remains the official definition.

Term Definition After-action Same-shift structured review of a triggered case (late DTN, DTD outlier, missed reversal or nimodipine, research-clock interference) that captures interval times and a recovery owner. aSAH Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. CSC volume eligibility uses the live E-App table; the April 2, 2025 Joint Commission announcement reduced the annual criterion to 10. ASPECTS Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score. Imaging estimate of early ischemic change used in EVT selection conversations; not a stand-alone treatment rule. ASRH Acute Stroke Ready Hospital. Entry-level Joint Commission advanced stroke program focused on initial evaluation, IVT when eligible, and rapid transfer. Abstractor Quality analyst who applies STK/CSTK/GWTG specifications to the medical record. The abstractor owns the definition; clinicians own the care. Academic measure KPI class that tracks capability-building (trial screens, fellow logs, scholarly output), not just clinical throughput. ACGME Program Director Fellowship PD. Distinct from the stroke program manager. Accepting physician Named CSC attending who accepts a transfer and starts the receiving-campus clock and capacity plan. Achievement measures The seven GWTG-Stroke measures that must each reach 85% for award eligibility (IVT timing, early antithrombotics, VTE, discharge antithrombotics, AF anticoagulation, smoking cessation, intensive statin). Advanced Therapy Target: Stroke published award cut: 50% door-to-device ≤90 min for direct arrivals and ≤60 min for transfers (minimum 6 patients). An award, not a CSC certification floor. Alteplase IV thrombolytic dosed 0.9 mg/kg, maximum 90 mg, 10% bolus and remainder over 60 minutes, in the 4.5-hour construct (2026 AIS guideline). AMD Associate Medical Director. Deputy who can chair weekly ops, take night escalation, and succeed the Medical Director without a coverage hole. Balancing measure Metric that detects harm from over-focusing on a process target (mimic overtriage, pharmacy near misses, fellow duty-hour violations, research-clock events). BAC Brain Attack Coalition. Issued 2000 PSC recommendations and the 2005 CSC consensus. Foundational history, not a substitute for current TJC standards. BAO Basilar-artery occlusion. Posterior-circulation EVT uses a local written rule; do not apply DAWN/DEFUSE cutoffs by habit. Bronze / Silver / Gold GWTG-Stroke achievement-award durations: 90 consecutive days, 12 months, and 24 months, each requiring 85% on all seven achievement measures. Bypass protocol EMS destination rule that may skip a nearer ASRH/PSC to reach EVT-capable care for suspected LVO. Must be regional, not campus folklore. Central IRB Single institutional review board used by multicenter networks (including StrokeNet). Academic CSCs treat familiarity as a research-operations skill. CDS / SaMD Clinical decision support / software as a medical device. January 2026 FDA CDS guidance is the current U.S. frame. CEA / CAS / TCAR Carotid endarterectomy / stenting / transcarotid artery revascularization. Code stroke Hospital-wide activation that assembles ED, imaging, pharmacy, vascular neurology, and IR standby for suspected acute stroke. Comfort measures Formal transition to comfort-focused care. A CSTK-01 exclusion when documented day of or day after arrival; must be clinical, not a biased shortcut. Coordinator FTE Funded research or program coordinator time. The hidden capacity behind 24/7 screening, abstraction, and 90-day calling. CSC Comprehensive Stroke Center. Most demanding Joint Commission advanced stroke program: full hyperacute, hemorrhagic, neurocritical, imaging, peer-review, research, and performance-measurement capability. CSTK Comprehensive Stroke measure set. v2026B (operational 3Q–4Q 2026) active IDs: CSTK-01 through CSTK-06 and CSTK-08 through CSTK-12. Same IDs in v2026A (1Q–2Q 2026) and v2027A (1Q–2Q 2027). CSTK-01 NIHSS performed for ischemic stroke before recanalization, or within 12 hours if no recanalization, with specified exclusions. CSTK-02 Modified Rankin Scale at 90 days. Production clock: enroll at discharge, first attempt by day 60, second by day 75, close in the specification window. CSTK-03 Severity measurement for SAH and ICH (overall). Hunt and Hess for SAH (03a); ICH Score for ICH (03b). Prior to surgery or within 6 hours of arrival if no surgery. WFNS and modified Fisher are clinical adjuncts, not the measure. Sampling: Yes. CSTK-04 Procoagulant reversal agent initiation for ICH. Confirm live MIF0289 for denominator and agents. Class-specific 2022 ICH reversal (idarucizumab, andexanet/PCC, protamine) is a clinical SOP, not automatically the CSTK-04 numerator. Does not apply to post-IVT hemorrhagic transformation (that is CSTK-05). CSTK-05 Hemorrhagic transformation (overall). CSTK-06 Nimodipine treatment administered (aSAH). First dose within 24 hours of arrival. Never give nimodipine IV (U.S. boxed warning). Clinical course commonly 60 mg q4h; hypotension adjustment is local. CSTK-07 Not in the current (v2026B) set. Do not list, audit, or poster as active. CSTK-08 TICI post-treatment reperfusion grade. CSTK-09 Arrival time to skin puncture (overall). Not door-to-device (first device pass). Different clocks. CSTK-10 mRS at 90 days — favorable-outcome construct. CSTK-11 TICI ≥2B within 120 minutes of hospital arrival. CSTK-12 TICI ≥2B within 60 minutes of skin puncture. CUSP AHRQ Comprehensive Unit-based Safety Program. Unit-level method pairing safety culture with teamwork tools. CVT / CVST Cerebral venous (sinus) thrombosis. 2024 AHA statement is the operational source. Not a standard GWTG ischemic / CSTK-01 row. CTA / CTP / MRA CT angiography, CT perfusion, and MR angiography. Vascular and tissue imaging used for LVO detection and selected extended-window decisions. DAPT Dual antiplatelet therapy. CHANCE/POINT inform use in selected minor non-disabling stroke/TIA; not a substitute for anticoagulation in AF. DAWN / DEFUSE 3 Landmark late-window EVT trials. DAWN clock is 6–24 h; DEFUSE 3 clock is 6–16 h. Do not collapse them to a single 6–24 h class. DCI Delayed cerebral ischemia after aSAH. DIDO Door-in-door-out. Time from arrival at the first hospital to departure for the CSC. A network reliability measure. Disabling deficit Clinically important neurologic deficit that qualifies for rapid IVT within 4.5 hours even if the NIHSS number is low (2026 AIS guideline). DMAIC Six Sigma sequence: Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control. Compatible with PDSA; does not replace a finished small cycle. Door-to-CT Interval from campus arrival to CT start. Local operational watch metric; not a published GWTG award threshold in this handbook. Door-to-device Arrival to first pass with the thrombectomy device. Not CSTK-09 puncture. See DTD. Drip-and-keep Spoke gives IVT and retains the patient when EVT or a higher-level bundle is not indicated. Drip-and-drive IVT at the spoke; the endovascular team travels. A design option, not a CSC mandate. Drip-and-ship Spoke gives IVT and transfers immediately for EVT or higher-level care. DSC Disease-Specific Care. Joint Commission certification framework with three components: standards, clinical practice guidelines, and performance measurement. DTD Door-to-device: arrival to first pass with the thrombectomy device. Target: Stroke Advanced Therapy uses ≤90 min direct / ≤60 min transfer. Not CSTK-09 (arrival to skin puncture). Different clocks. DTN Door-to-needle. Time from arrival to IV thrombolytic administration. Target: Stroke tiers use 60 / 45 / 30 minute cuts. Dual-eligible Patient who meets criteria for both IVT and EVT and should receive both rapidly, without delaying thrombectomy. DWI-FLAIR mismatch MRI pattern used to select some unknown-onset patients for extended-window IVT. E-App Joint Commission electronic application / eligibility tables. The live source for current CSC volume criteria. Confirm rather than memorize. Elite Target: Stroke Honor Roll Elite: 85% of applicable patients with DTN ≤60 minutes. A published award cut, not a CSC certification floor. Elite Plus Target: Stroke Honor Roll Elite Plus: 75% DTN ≤45 minutes and 50% DTN ≤30 minutes. A published award cut, not a CSC certification floor. Elective carotid intervention CSTK-01 exclusion when the intervention is the reason for admission. EMS prenotification Pre-arrival notice from emergency medical services that starts team assembly before the patient crosses the door. EMTALA Recipient-hospital obligation: a CSC with specialized capability must accept an appropriate transfer if it has the capacity to treat. No payor screen. See Chapter 19. Equity measure KPI slice that tests whether reliability is the same by night/weekend, transfer status, language, sex, race/ethnicity, or payor. ESUS Embolic stroke of undetermined source. A workup state, not a final diagnosis. EVD External ventricular drain. EVT Endovascular therapy (mechanical thrombectomy / MER) for selected ischemic stroke, typically LVO. Extended-window IVT IVT beyond 4.5 hours or for unknown onset in selected patients using DWI-FLAIR or perfusion mismatch (2026 AIS guideline). Favorable outcome In CSTK-10, the specified favorable 90-day mRS construct. In HERMES reporting, often mRS 0–2 — do not mix the two without labeling. Fellowship (vascular neurology) ACGME-accredited training program. A CSC education pillar, not an optional academic extra. Fever AIS: treat temperatures >37.5 °C to achieve normothermia (2026 AIS §4.4). ICH INTERACT3 trial-bundle uses ≤37.5 °C. Operationally both mean treat at >37.5. Do not use 38.0 as an AIS cut. Floor vs internal target Three classes, not two. Certification floor = live DSC / CSC eligibility or measure specification. Published award cut = Honor Roll / Elite / Elite Plus / Advanced Therapy or GWTG achievement as posted. Internal aim = local management goal, labeled internal. Do not collapse the three. FPPE / OPPE Focused and Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation. Medical-staff processes that must use the same case file the quality committee trusts. FTE Full-time equivalent. The worksheet unit for Medical Director, AMD, abstractor, caller, coordinator, and related roles. GWTG-Stroke Get With The Guidelines–Stroke. AHA quality program and recognition pathway built on achievement and quality measures. Hemorrhagic transformation Post-reperfusion or spontaneous bleed into an infarct; CSTK-05 reports the overall measure. HERMES 2016 patient-level meta-analysis of the pivotal EVT trials. mRS 0–2 46.0% vs 26.5%; NNT 2.6 for ≥1-point mRS shift. Honor Roll Target: Stroke Honor Roll: 75% DTN ≤60 minutes (minimum 6 patients). A published award cut, not a CSC certification floor. HRO High-reliability organizing. Five principles: preoccupation with failure, reluctance to simplify, sensitivity to operations, commitment to resilience, deference to expertise. Hub-and-spoke Network model with a CSC hub and ASRH/PSC/TSC spokes connected by EMS, telestroke, and transfer rules. Hunt-Hess / WFNS Hunt and Hess is the CSTK-03 instrument for SAH (03a). WFNS and modified Fisher are clinical adjuncts, not the measure. ICH Score is the CSTK-03 instrument for ICH (03b). ICH Intracerebral hemorrhage. Operational source: 2022 AHA/ASA ICH guideline; reversal initiation is CSTK-04. ICH score Common ICH severity tool used toward CSTK-03. IHI Model for Improvement Aim, measures, changes, then PDSA cycles. Default small-cycle method in this handbook. In-hospital / in-house stroke Stroke that begins after arrival, including perioperative. Separate denominator from ED-arrival codes; last-known-well still rules. See Chapter 43. INTERACT / ENCHANTED2 ICH care-bundle trials that inform bundled blood-pressure and supportive-care operations. IVT Intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase). Just culture Accountability model distinguishing human error, at-risk behavior, and reckless behavior. Large-core EVT Thrombectomy in selected patients with large ischemic core (SELECT2, ANGEL-ASPECT, RESCUE-Japan LIMIT). Local protocol must define eligibility. Last known well (LKW) Time the patient was last observed at neurologic baseline. The clock that all hyperacute decisions reference. Leadership designee After-hours owner of the decision-rights matrix. Lean Waste-reduction improvement method. Compatible with PDSA when the change is still small enough to finish. LVO Large-vessel occlusion. Typical anatomic target for EVT. MER Mechanical endovascular reperfusion. Joint Commission language family that includes IA/MER populations in CSTK. Mimic Non-stroke diagnosis that entered the code-stroke pathway. A balancing-measure population. Mothership EMS transports a suspected LVO candidate directly to an EVT-capable center rather than the nearest hospital. mRS Modified Rankin Scale. Functional outcome scored 0–6; required at 90 days for CSTK-02/10. mRS 90-day clock Enroll at discharge, first attempt by day 60, second by day 75, close in the specification window. MSU Mobile stroke unit. Ambulance with imaging and treatment capability; endorsed in the 2026 AIS guideline. NCC Neurocritical care. Dedicated neuro ICU capability is a historical and operational CSC expectation. NIHSS National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale. Required for CSTK-01 as specified. Does not, by itself, exclude a disabling deficit from 4.5-hour IVT. Nimodipine Standard aSAH medication; CSTK-06 clocks first dose within 24 hours of arrival. Never give nimodipine IV (U.S. boxed warning). Clinical course commonly 60 mg q4h; hypotension adjustment is local. 2023 aSAH guideline is the operational source. NIR Neurointerventional radiology / endovascular neurosurgery service that performs EVT and selected aneurysm procedures. NNT Number needed to treat. HERMES reported NNT 2.6 for ≥1-point mRS shift with EVT vs control. On-call escalation card Pocket-level page tree stating who is called, in what order, for code stroke, IR, reversal, transfer pressure, and stop-the-line. Operating rhythm Daily huddle → weekly ops → monthly quality → quarterly stroke executive. After-action is a triggered ritual, not a fifth standing forum. Operating-system card One-page map of pillar owners, standing meetings, defect-routing rules, and stop-the-line authority. Outcome measure KPI that tracks what happened to the patient (90-day mRS, symptomatic HT, mortality — the last labeled if unadjusted). PDSA Plan-Do-Study-Act. One-page improvement cycle with a numeric prediction and a 90-day kill/close date. Pediatric AIS Childhood acute ischemic stroke. First dedicated recommendations appear in the 2026 AIS guideline. Peer review Privileged case review for quality and professionalism. Must have a path that the night team can find. Performance measurement The DSC component that includes STK/CSTK (and related) reporting. Not optional for CSC. Perfusion mismatch Imaging pattern used to select some 4.5–9 hour or unknown-onset patients for IVT or late-window EVT. PFO Patent foramen ovale. Closure evaluation is a clinic/cardiology pathway, not a day-2 implant. Plus award GWTG recognition that adds quality-measure compliance on top of the seven achievement measures. Process measure KPI that tracks whether the right action happened on time (DTN, CSTK-09, STK-5). Procoagulant reversal Timed initiation of agents that reverse anticoagulation or coagulopathy in ICH (CSTK-04). PSC Primary Stroke Center. Joint Commission advanced program with IVT and organized inpatient stroke care; transfers complex cases. RACI Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed. Decision-rights grid used so pillars do not collide. Recanalization / reperfusion Opening of an occluded vessel / restoration of flow. TICI grades reperfusion after EVT. Research-clock event Any trial screen, consent, or coordinator action that adds documented minutes to needle or puncture. Internal target is zero. SCS26 2026 Stroke Certification Standards book. Confirm live when quoting standards language. Site PI Site principal investigator. The physician owner of a trial at the CSC; a StrokeNet capability requirement. Skin puncture Time of arterial puncture for EVT. Start of the CSTK-12 interval. SOP Standard operating procedure. Handbook skeletons are samples until locally approved. Spoke Referring hospital in the hub-and-spoke network (ASRH, PSC, TSC, or undesignated). STK Inpatient stroke core measure set: STK-1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10. STK-OP Outpatient/ED stroke measure family in v2026B. Confirm current specifications. STK-3 Anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation/flutter at discharge (also GWTG achievement measure 5). STK-4 Inpatient thrombolytic-therapy measure. Do not confuse with Target: Stroke DTN. STK-6 Discharged on statin per the STK specification. Not the same as the GWTG achievement intensive-statin measure. Stop-the-line Authority of any clinician to halt an unsafe step (wrong dose card, stock-out, research interference) and escalate the same shift. StrokeNet NIH national network for multicenter stroke trials in acute care, prevention, and recovery. StrokeNet National Coordinating Center StrokeNet’s national clinical coordinating hub. Do not abbreviate as NCC in CSC documents; NCC means neurocritical care. Stroke program manager RN/operational dyad partner. Distinct from the ACGME Program Director. Structural measure KPI that asks whether the system can still run Tuesday night (call coverage, stock, abstractor backlog, rolling volumes). Survey tracer Surveyor method that follows one patient through people, documents, and time stamps rather than through an org chart. SWOT Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats. Offsite tool that must translate into bets or a parked list. Target: Stroke AHA time-based recognition program (Honor Roll, Elite, Elite Plus, Advanced Therapy). Phase III national goals match Elite / Advanced Therapy primary goals. Each tier is a published award cut, not a CSC certification floor. Target: Type 2 Diabetes GWTG composite recognition requiring ≥80% for 12 months. Teach-back Patient demonstrates understanding of STK-8 content. Telestroke Remote vascular-neurology evaluation that issues a time-critical recommendation and, when indicated, a transfer decision. Tenecteplase (TNK) IV thrombolytic dosed 0.25 mg/kg IV push, maximum 25 mg (2026 AIS guideline; EXTEND-IA TNK). 0.4 mg/kg is not recommended (Class 3 – No Benefit). Do not use a coronary-dose card. TICI Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction scale. CSTK-08 documents the grade; CSTK-11/12 use TICI ≥2B as effective reperfusion. TIA Transient ischemic attack. Disposition follows the 2021 secondary-prevention guideline; do not invent an ABCD2 cutoff here. Tracer script Pre-written walkthrough of IVT, transfer EVT, ICH reversal, aSAH nimodipine, or 90-day mRS used in mock and real surveys. Transfer center 24/7 intake function that runs the transfer checklist, names the accepting physician, and never leaves a sender without a next step. TSC Thrombectomy-Capable Stroke Center. Joint Commission advanced program with 24/7 EVT but not the full CSC portfolio. Unknown-onset / wake-up stroke Stroke with unclear LKW. May qualify for extended-window IVT or late-window EVT under imaging-based local protocols. Vascular neurology Physician specialty that owns the medical stroke service, code-stroke decision, and typically the Medical Director role. VTE prophylaxis Venous thromboembolism prevention. STK-1 and GWTG achievement measure 3.

Related files: Evidence Register for sourced numbers; Living Document Protocol when a definition must change.

docs.title: Opening
docs.text: This is a working handbook, not a monograph to be read once. Use it the way an operations leader uses a flight manual: open the chapter that matches the problem in front of you, adapt the tools, and return when the system changes.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
The primary reader is the Medical Director or Associate Medical Director of a U.S. academic Comprehensive Stroke Center. Secondary readers include stroke program directors (nursing/operational), quality directors, neurocritical care and endovascular partners, department chairs, and hospital executives who sponsor the CSC.

The scope is deliberately narrow:

  • U.S. academic CSCs only
  • Public standards, guidelines, and high-level operating principles
  • No proprietary data from any named institution
  • No individual attribution

docs.title: How the book is organized
docs.text:
Part Use it when you need to I Foundations Explain what a CSC is, what certification actually requires, and how the regional system works II Leadership Design authority, committees, FTE, culture, and succession III Clinical enterprise Build or repair a specific clinical pathway from EMS to rehab IV Quality and safety Stand up data, metrics, improvement methods, surveys, and equity work V Education Run fellowship, GME, interprofessional, and community education VI Research Build trials infrastructure, faculty pipelines, and governed innovation VII Strategy Grow, finance, network, prepare for surge, and pursue elite standing VIII Playbooks Implement in 90 days, copy templates, and run the operating cadence

Special-population operations — cerebral venous thrombosis, maternal stroke, and pediatric receiving — live in Chapter 42. Chapters 43–46 cover in-hospital stroke, goals of care, the TIA clinic, and elective cerebrovascular operations.

docs.title: How to read a chapter
docs.text:
Every chapter follows the same operating logic:

  1. Opening — the job to be done
  2. Why this matters — clinical, regulatory, and organizational stakes
  3. Core framework — the model, standards, and decision rights
  4. How to do the work — daily, weekly, quarterly, and multi-year actions
  5. Ready-to-adapt tools — checklists, agendas, scorecards, SOP skeletons
  6. Sources — primary citations with enough specificity to re-verify

Callouts are used with a fixed meaning:

Key Actions

What the Medical Director should do this week or this quarter.

Metrics Targets

The numbers used to manage the work. Certification requirements and published award criteria (Honor Roll / Elite / Elite Plus / Advanced Therapy) are labeled as such. Internal aims are labeled internal.

Common Pitfalls

Failure modes seen in academic CSCs: authority without control, vanity metrics, survey theater, and ungoverned growth.

Implementation Tips

Practical sequencing, coalition-building, and how to make a change survive contact with the EHR, the OR board, and the night float.

docs.title: How to treat evidence
docs.text:
Standards and guidelines move. The Evidence Register records the primary sources behind high-consequence claims and the date they were last verified. The Living Document Protocol is the monthly maintenance loop.

When a local protocol and a national guideline diverge, the handbook tells you what the national source currently says and how to document a local exception. It does not invent institutional policy.

docs.title: How to adapt tools
docs.text: Templates in Part VIII are generic and original. Replace bracketed fields, align with medical staff bylaws and hospital policy, and route SOPs through monthly quality and charter language through quarterly stroke executive before implementation. Do not paste a sample SOP into production without local legal, pharmacy, radiology, and nursing review.

docs.title: Navigation conventions
docs.text:
• The left rail is the table of contents.
  • The right rail is the page outline.
  • Search covers the full handbook.
  • Mermaid diagrams are operating pictures, not decorative art. If a diagram and the surrounding table disagree, trust the table and file a currency issue.

docs.title: What this handbook will not do
docs.text: It will not name a person, a hospital, or a health system as the source of a practice. It will not substitute for medical staff privileging, legal review, or a live reading of the current Joint Commission manual. It will not treat last year's award as this year's performance.

docs.title: Living Document and Monthly Update Protocol
Opening
docs.text:
Standards, measures, and trial evidence move. A handbook that does not have a maintenance system becomes a liability. This protocol is the operating procedure for keeping Comprehensive Stroke Center Management current without rewriting it from scratch each month.

The unit of work is a currency drop: a dated, scoped set of source checks, chapter patches, evidence-register updates, and a changelog entry. The unit of time is the first week of each month. The unit of quality is mkdocs build --strict plus a hard filter for forbidden strings.

docs.title: Why This Matters
docs.text: Medical Directors will use these pages in survey week, in a 90-day plan, and in a board packet. A stale CSTK ID, an obsolete aSAH volume criterion, or a pre-2026 thrombolytic recommendation is worse than a missing paragraph. Currency is part of the product.

docs.title: Core Framework
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[First of month] --> B[Re-open primary sources]
    B --> C{Any claim changed?}
    C -->|No| D[Stamp last-verified dates]
    C -->|Yes| E[Patch chapters]
    E --> F[Update evidence register]
    D --> G[Changelog entry]
    F --> G
    G --> H[Strict build]
    H --> I[Forbidden-string filter]
    I --> J[Publish]
Cadence Work Owner Monthly (1st) Source re-verification and dated register stamps Handbook maintainer / automated reminder issue Same week Chapter patches only where claims moved Maintainer Same week Changelog YYYY.MM entry Maintainer Ad hoc Mid-month correction if a major guideline or measure set drops Maintainer Annual Full TOC and toolkit review Maintainer

Key Actions

On the first business day of the month, open the GitHub Actions evidence-currency issue, walk the source list below, and do not close the issue until the register dates and changelog are updated.

Metrics Targets

100% of high-consequence rows in the Evidence Register have a last-verified date no older than 45 days. Zero unresolved “needs confirmation” rows on doses, time targets, or active measure IDs.

Common Pitfalls

Rewriting chapters that did not change. Updating a table but not the surrounding prose. Leaving a historical volume number unmarked. Shipping a currency drop that fails --strict because a renamed file broke navigation.

Implementation Tips

Prefer a surgical patch of the sentence and the register row over a stylistic rewrite. If a source is paywalled or the live manual is version-gated, record that fact and keep the prior extraction labeled “confirm current.”

docs.title: Sources to re-open every month
docs.text:
1. Joint Commission
  2. Stroke certification landing page and CSC eligibility notes
  3. Specifications Manual for National Quality Measures — CSTK and STK / STK-OP (current version code, e.g. v2026B)
  4. Disease-Specific Care / Stroke Certification Standards book year (SCS26 and successors)
  5. E-App / CSC eligibility table (dated screenshot). Confirm the aSAH volume criterion against the live table; the April 2, 2025 announcement reduced it to 10
  6. Any Joint Commission Online announcement on volume criteria
  7. AHA/ASA
  8. 2026 AIS guideline page and any subsequent correction
  9. 2022 ICH guideline and 2024 ICH performance measures
  10. 2023 aSAH guideline
  11. Secondary prevention and systems-of-care statements
  12. GWTG-Stroke
  13. Recognition criteria page (achievement measures; Target: Stroke tiers; Target: Type 2 Diabetes)
  14. CMS
  15. Hospital IQR / OQR measure lists that mention stroke
  16. NIH StrokeNet
  17. Network structure and any operational changes that affect site readiness
  18. Landmark trial results published since the last drop that change pathway design (EVT windows, ICH bundles, thrombolytic choice)

docs.title: How to patch a chapter
docs.text:
1. Identify the claim and its evidence-register ID.
  2. Open the primary source. Extract population, intervention, comparator, endpoint, and number.
  3. Change the smallest block of prose and the matching table cell.
  4. If a measure is retired, remove it from active tables and add a one-line historical note.
  5. If a new measure appears, add it to Core Metrics and the Evidence Register.
  6. Do not introduce personal names of handbook creators or individual affiliations while editing. Run the repository-root AGENTS.md hard-filter before merge.

docs.title: How to add an evidence-register row
docs.text:
Use the live register columns (do not invent a second schema):

ID Claim Chapter Primary source Verified extraction Last verified Status ER-DOMAIN-## One-sentence operational claim Chapter slugs Full citation + DOI or URL Exact number or wording extracted YYYY-MM-DD active / confirm live / historical / retired

Promote a row to active only when the extraction has been re-read from the primary source. Use confirm live when the public page is incomplete or the live manual is version-gated (E-App volume tables, CMS OQR). Never recycle a retired ID.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
• Monthly currency drop: YYYY.MM (example: 2026.08)
  • Same-month correction: YYYY.MM.N (example: 2026.08.1)
  • Record every drop in Changelog

docs.title: First-of-month checklist
docs.text:
• Open or refresh the evidence-currency GitHub issue
  • Re-open the six source classes above
  • Diff each high-consequence register row against the live source
  • Patch affected chapters
  • Update last-verified dates
  • Write the changelog entry
  • Run mkdocs build --strict
  • Run the hard-filter listed in repository-root AGENTS.md
  • Merge and confirm Pages deploy

docs.title: Prompt library
docs.text: Ready-to-run prompts live in the repository-root file AGENTS.md (not a published handbook page). Copy the Monthly evidence-refresh prompt into a new session on the first of the month. Use the targeted re-swarm prompts in that same file when only one pillar moved (clinical operations; quality and certification; education and research; strategy; visual and template polish).

docs.title: Daily / weekly
docs.text: No standing weekly currency work unless a guideline or measure set is released mid-cycle. If one is released, open an ad hoc issue the same day.

docs.title: Monthly / quarterly
docs.text: Execute the first-of-month checklist. Once per quarter, read Part VIII templates to ensure sample SOPs still match current doses and measure IDs.

docs.title: Annual / multi-year
docs.text: Re-evaluate the table of contents. Retire chapters that no longer earn their place. Add chapters only when a durable new CSC capability appears (for example, a new certification tier or a practice-changing care model).

docs.title: Integration With Other Pillars
docs.text: Currency is not a back-matter hobby. A changed thrombolytic recommendation must land in IV thrombolysis, hyperacute pathways, core metrics, and the SOP skeletons in KPI and SOP templates in the same drop.

docs.text:
